cards.en:
Analogy: imagine every object at home could "talk": the fridge tells your phone the milk is finished, the aircon hears you are coming home. That talking network of things is the Internet of Things (IoT).

How it works

  • Sensor = a part that measures something (temperature, location, motion).
  • The object sends the data through a wireless technology: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, RFID (Radio Frequency Identification, a tag read by radio) or NFC (Near Field Communication, very short range, e.g. tapping a card).
  • IoT makes a huge amount of data every second, so it is stored and processed by cloud computing.
  • Based on the result, objects take actions automatically.

Examples: smart speakers, smart homes (lights/aircon controlled remotely), smart bands, cars sending speed and location for real-time arrival time.

Exam wording: IoT refers to a network connecting different objects. The connected objects share collected data and provide new functionalities. IoT collects the data; cloud computing stores and processes it in real time; objects then act automatically.
cards.zh:
比喻：如果家里每样东西都会“说话”：雪柜告诉手机牛奶没了，冷气知道你快到家。这个会说话的物件网络就是 Internet of Things (IoT，物联网)。

运作

  • Sensor（感应器）= 量度东西的部件（温度、位置、动作）。
  • 物件用无线技术传数据：Wi-Fi、Bluetooth、RFID（无线射频识别标签）、NFC（近场通讯，极短距离，例如拍卡）。
  • IoT 每秒产生大量数据，要靠 cloud computing 储存及处理。
  • 按处理结果，物件自动采取行动。

例子：智能喇叭、智能家居、智能手环、车辆传速度和位置计算预计到达时间。

考试写法：IoT refers to a network connecting different objects. The connected objects share collected data and provide new functionalities. IoT 收集数据，cloud 储存及实时分析，物件再自动行动。

ex.q: A smart aircon turns on when the owner's phone is within 1 km of home. Identify the IoT elements.
ex.a:
1. Connected objects: phone and aircon.
2. Data collected: the phone's GPS location.
3. Network: location sent by mobile data / Wi-Fi to a cloud server.
4. Processing: cloud checks if distance < 1 km.
5. Action: server sends a command, aircon switches on automatically.
ex.az:
1. 物件：手机和冷气。
2. 数据：手机 GPS 位置。
3. 经流动数据／Wi-Fi 送到云端。
4. 云端判断距离是否少于 1 km。
5. 发指令，冷气自动开。

ex.q: Explain why IoT relies on cloud computing.
ex.a:
1. IoT devices produce a huge amount of data every second.
2. The devices themselves have little storage and processing power.
3. Cloud servers can store and process the data through the Internet instantly.
4. So results come back in real time and devices can act automatically.
ex.az:
1. IoT 每秒产生大量数据。
2. 装置本身储存和运算能力小。
3. 云端可经 Internet 即时储存及处理。
4. 所以能实时回传结果，自动行动。

ex.q: A student writes: "A smart band is IoT because it has a screen." What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Having a screen is not what makes it IoT.
2. It is IoT because it is connected: it collects data (heart rate, steps) and shares it over Bluetooth to a phone/cloud, giving new functions (health reports).
3. Right answer: mention collect data + share through a network + new functionality.
ex.az:
1. 有屏幕不是 IoT 的原因。
2. 它是 IoT 因为连网：收集心率步数，经 Bluetooth 分享到手机／云端，提供新功能。
3. 要写：收集数据 + 经网络分享 + 新功能。

demo.title: IoT flow: smart aircon

frames.en: The phone's GPS sensor reads its location.
frames.zh: 手机 GPS 感应器读取位置。

frames.en: Data goes out over Wi-Fi / mobile network.
frames.zh: 数据经 Wi-Fi／流动网络传出。

frames.en: The cloud server stores the data and checks: distance < 1 km?
frames.zh: 云端储存数据并判断：距离 < 1 km？

frames.en: Cloud sends a command; the aircon switches on and the phone gets a notice.
frames.zh: 云端发指令，冷气自动开，手机收到通知。

cards.en:
Analogy: instead of keeping all your money under your bed, you put it in a bank and use it from any ATM. The cloud is the bank for your files and programs.

How it works: the cloud simply means the Internet. Data and programs are kept on remote servers hosted by a third party (the provider) and you reach them through the Internet. You don't need to upgrade your hardware or install lots of software.

BenefitMeaning
AccessibilityAccess data anywhere, anytime via the Internet
FlexibilityChange service plan on demand (e.g. buy more storage)
MaintenanceProvider handles maintenance, backup and upgrades

Limitations: needs an Internet connection; data kept by a third party (privacy/security concerns); ongoing subscription fees.

Exam wording: Everything in the cloud is stored in remote servers hosted by a third party and is accessible through the Internet.
cards.zh:
比喻：钱不放床底而放银行，在任何提款机都能用。Cloud 就是你文件和程式的“银行”。

运作：cloud 就是 Internet。数据和程式放在第三方托管的远端伺服器，经 Internet 使用，不用升级硬件或安装大量软件。

好处意思
Accessibility随时随地经 Internet 存取
Flexibility按需要改计划（如加空间）
Maintenance维护、备份、升级由供应商负责

限制：要连网；数据交第三方（私隐／保安）；持续月费。

考试写法：Everything in the cloud is stored in remote servers hosted by a third party and is accessible through the Internet.

ex.q: A school moves homework from a local file server to cloud storage. Give two benefits and one drawback.
ex.a:
1. Accessibility: students hand in/read homework anytime, anywhere.
2. Maintenance: the provider does backup and upgrades, saving the school's IT work.
3. Drawback: no Internet = no access; or data held by a third party raises privacy concerns.
ex.az:
1. 随时随地存取。
2. 维护备份由供应商负责。
3. 缺点：断网用不到／数据交第三方有私隐问题。

ex.q: A shop's online storage is full in December. Which cloud benefit helps?
ex.a:
1. Flexibility.
2. The shop can upgrade the plan on demand to get more storage at once.
3. No need to buy and install new hard disks.
ex.az:
1. Flexibility。
2. 可即时加购空间。
3. 不用买新硬碟。

ex.q: A student says: "Cloud data is safe because it is not on my computer." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Wrong: being off your computer does not make data safe.
2. The data sits on a third party's servers and travels over the Internet, so there are privacy and security concerns (leaks, hacking).
3. Correct view: cloud gives backup by the provider, but you still need strong passwords / 2FA.
ex.az:
1. 错：不在自己电脑不等于安全。
2. 数据在第三方伺服器并经 Internet 传送，有私隐及保安风险。
3. 正确：供应商有备份，但仍要强密码／2FA。

demo.title: What 'the cloud' really is

frames.en: You use a laptop and a phone.
frames.zh: 你用手提电脑和手机。

frames.en: Both connect through the Internet.
frames.zh: 两者经 Internet 连接。

frames.en: Files live on the provider's servers, so any device sees the same latest copy.
frames.zh: 文件在供应商伺服器，任何装置看到同一最新版本。

cards.en:
Analogy: renting from a cloud is like renting at a hotel: you can rent the whole room (a computer), just a locker (storage), or use the gym (a ready app).

TypeWhat you rentExamples
Operating system (virtual machines)Run tasks on more powerful virtual machines (a computer simulated by software on the server)Microsoft Azure, Google Compute Engine
StorageStore data on remote servers hosted by a third partyGoogle Drive, OneDrive, iCloud
Hosted applicationOpen and use software from the cloud server without installing itGoogle Docs Editors, Office 365

Cloud also powers collaboration tools: users share and co-edit files in real time.

Exam wording: name the type, then say what is on the server: "the program runs on the cloud server, so no installation is needed on the local computer".
cards.zh:
比喻：像住酒店：可以租整间房（一部电脑）、只租储物柜（储存）、或用现成健身室（应用程式）。

类型租什么例子
Operating system (virtual machines)在云端更强的虚拟机（软件模拟的电脑）运行工作Azure、Google Compute Engine
Storage数据放第三方伺服器Google Drive、OneDrive、iCloud
Hosted application在云端直接用软件，不用安装Google Docs、Office 365

云端亦支援协作工具：多人实时共同编辑。

考试写法：写出类型，再写 the program runs on the cloud server, so no installation is needed。

ex.q: Classify: (i) renting a powerful server to train a model; (ii) backing up photos to iCloud; (iii) writing an essay in Google Docs.
ex.a:
1. (i) needs computing power → virtual machine / OS service.
2. (ii) only keeps files → storage.
3. (iii) software used in browser without install → hosted application.
ex.az:
1. 要运算力 → 虚拟机。
2. 只存文件 → 储存。
3. 浏览器内用软件 → 托管应用。

ex.q: A low-spec Chromebook can still edit spreadsheets in Office 365. Why?
ex.a:
1. Office 365 is a hosted application.
2. The program runs on the cloud server; the Chromebook only shows the result in a browser.
3. So the local computer needs no installation and little power.
ex.az:
1. Office 365 是托管应用。
2. 程式在云端运行，本机只显示。
3. 所以本机不用安装、要求低。

ex.q: A student classifies Google Drive as a hosted application because "it is used in a browser". Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Using a browser is not the test.
2. Google Drive's main job is to keep files on remote servers → storage.
3. Google Docs (the editor) is the hosted application.
ex.az:
1. 用浏览器不是判断标准。
2. Drive 主要存文件 → storage。
3. Google Docs 编辑器才是 hosted application。

cards.en:
Analogy: a USB drive is like passing one notebook around the class; a cloud document is like a big whiteboard everyone can write on at the same time.

A group project could use (1) a USB drive passed around, (2) meeting after school while one person types, or (3) cloud-based document editing (e.g. Google Docs).

Cloud collaborationUSB / meeting
Edit simultaneously in real time, anywhereOne person edits at a time / must meet at same place and time
Only one up-to-date versionMany copies → version conflicts
Saved automatically, version history, commentsUSB can be lost or spread malware

Exam wording: "Members can edit the same document simultaneously in real time; there is only one up-to-date version, avoiding version inconsistency."
cards.zh:
比喻：USB 像全班轮流传一本簿；云端文件像一块大白板，大家可同时写。

小组项目方法：(1) USB 轮流传；(2) 放学见面一人打字；(3) 云端文件（Google Docs）。

云端协作USB／见面
多人同时实时编辑，随地可用一次一人／要同时同地
只有一个最新版本多个副本 → 版本混乱
自动储存、版本纪录、留言USB 会遗失或带病毒

考试写法：Members can edit the same document simultaneously in real time; there is only one up-to-date version, avoiding version inconsistency.

ex.q: Give two disadvantages of circulating a USB drive compared with cloud collaboration.
ex.a:
1. Only one member can edit at a time, so progress is slow.
2. Several copies exist, causing version inconsistency.
3. (Also accepted) the USB may be lost or spread malware.
ex.az:
1. 一次一人，慢。
2. 多个副本，版本不一致。
3. USB 可遗失／带病毒。

ex.q: A member deletes a paragraph by accident in a shared Google Doc. How can the group recover it?
ex.a:
1. Open the document's version history.
2. Find the version before the deletion.
3. Restore it (or copy the paragraph back).
ex.az:
1. 打开版本纪录。
2. 找删除前的版本。
3. 还原。

ex.q: A student says cloud collaboration works without Internet because the file is saved automatically. Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Wrong: real-time co-editing and auto-save to the server need an Internet connection.
2. Offline edits (if allowed) only sync when back online.
3. So a limitation of cloud collaboration is: requires Internet access.
ex.az:
1. 错：实时协作及自动存到伺服器要连网。
2. 离线修改要上线后才同步。
3. 限制：需要 Internet。

demo.title: Three ways to do a group project

frames.en: A → B → C: one person edits, then passes the drive. Copies multiply.
frames.zh: A→B→C 轮流，一次一人，副本越来越多。

frames.en: Everyone must be in the same place at the same time; one person types.
frames.zh: 要同时同地，一人打字。

frames.en: All members edit the single file on the server at the same time.
frames.zh: 所有人同时编辑伺服器上同一文件。

cards.en:
Analogy: a city that works like a body: sensors are the eyes, the network is the nerves, the cloud + AI is the brain, and traffic lights or street lights are the hands.

How it works: cloud-based IoT applications enabled smart cities. A smart city is a complex system of systems: connected systems use IoT data and take actions based on AI analysis. Goal: make better decisions and improve quality of life by addressing urbanisation challenges (environment, traffic congestion, waste management).

Hong Kong's Smart City Blueprint: Smart Economy, Smart Living, Smart Mobility, Smart Environment, Smart People, Smart Government.

Exam wording: sensors collect data → sent to cloud → analysed → automatic action in real time → name the area (e.g. Smart Mobility).
cards.zh:
比喻：城市像身体：感应器是眼睛，网络是神经，cloud + AI 是大脑，交通灯和街灯是手。

运作：云端 IoT 应用推动智慧城市。智慧城市是系统中的系统：互连系统用 IoT 数据，按 AI 分析行动，目的是改善决策和生活质素，应对城市化问题（环境、塞车、废物）。

香港六范畴：Smart Economy、Living、Mobility、Environment、People、Government。

考试写法：感应器收集 → 送云端 → 分析 → 实时自动行动 → 写出范畴。

ex.q: Explain how a smart traffic light system is a smart city application.
ex.a:
1. Detectors (IoT) count vehicles and pedestrians.
2. Data is sent to the cloud.
3. AI analysis adjusts green-light time in real time.
4. Congestion drops → Smart Mobility.
ex.az:
1. 侦测器数车和人。
2. 送云端。
3. AI 实时调整绿灯。
4. 减少塞车 → Smart Mobility。

ex.q: Which area does a bin fill-level sensor belong to, and how does it help?
ex.a:
1. Smart Environment.
2. Sensors report how full each bin is.
3. The system plans collection routes to only visit full bins → less fuel and time.
ex.az:
1. Smart Environment。
2. 感应器回报满载程度。
3. 只收满的桶，省油省时。

ex.q: A student says: "A smart city means every citizen has a smartphone." What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Phones alone are not a smart city.
2. The key is connected systems using IoT data + AI analysis to act and solve urban problems.
3. Rewrite: "a system of systems that uses IoT data to make better decisions and improve quality of life".
ex.az:
1. 只有手机不算。
2. 关键是互连系统用 IoT 数据及 AI 行动解决城市问题。
3. 改写为“系统中的系统……改善生活质素”。

demo.title: Smart traffic light (system of systems)

frames.en: Road sensors count cars and pedestrians at the junction.
frames.zh: 路口感应器数车和行人。

frames.en: Cloud AI compares flows from many junctions.
frames.zh: 云端 AI 比较多个路口的流量。

frames.en: Green time is lengthened for the busy direction, in real time.
frames.zh: 实时延长繁忙方向的绿灯。

cards.t: Smart Economy: online banking and payment
cards.tz: 智慧经济：网上银行与支付
cards.en:
Analogy: your money becomes a message: instead of handing over coins, your phone sends "pay $30 to this shop" to the bank.

  • Online banking: check up-to-date transactions (no waiting for the monthly statement), transfer money, pay bills 24/7.
  • Online payment platforms (PayPal, FPS = Faster Payment System, PPS): pay over the Internet; top up a digital wallet (stored-value account in an app) or link to a credit card / bank account. This boosted online shops and start-ups.
  • Contactless payment: Octopus card (NFC), credit/debit card (magnetic stripe, chip, NFC), mobile wallet (NFC, QR code).

Drawback: a shop that accepts only e-payment loses cash customers and may widen the digital divide (gap between people who can and cannot use IT).

Exam wording: "faster, contactless payment; no need to handle cash" vs "customers who prefer cash cannot pay; widens the digital divide".
cards.zh:
比喻：钱变成讯息：手机通知银行“付 $30 给这间店”。

  • Online banking：随时看最新交易（不用等月结单）、转账、缴费。
  • Online payment（PayPal、转数快 FPS、PPS）：网上付款；可增值 digital wallet（app 内储值户口）或连信用卡／银行，推动网店。
  • Contactless payment：八达通（NFC）、信用卡（磁带、晶片、NFC）、手机钱包（NFC、QR code）。

缺点：只收电子支付会失去用现金的顾客，扩大数码鸿沟（会用与不会用 IT 的人之间的差距）。

考试写法：faster, contactless payment; no need to handle cash 对 customers who prefer cash cannot pay; widens the digital divide。

ex.q: A restaurant's ticket machine accepts only cards and mobile payment. One advantage, one disadvantage.
ex.a:
1. Advantage: faster, contactless, no handling of cash/change, fewer staff.
2. Disadvantage: customers who prefer cash (e.g. elderly) cannot pay → fewer sales, wider digital divide.
ex.az:
1. 好处：快、免找续、省人手。
2. 坏处：只用现金的顾客不能付 → 少生意、扩大数码鸿沟。

ex.q: Name the technology used: (i) tapping Octopus; (ii) paying by scanning the shop's code with a phone.
ex.a:
1. (i) NFC.
2. (ii) QR code.
ex.az:
1. NFC。
2. QR code。

ex.q: A student writes "online banking is better because you get the monthly statement faster". Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Online banking does not speed up the statement.
2. Its point is you can see up-to-date transactions anytime, without waiting for the monthly statement.
3. Also: transfer and pay bills 24/7.
ex.az:
1. 不是月结单更快。
2. 而是随时查看最新交易，毋须等月结单。
3. 亦可 24/7 转账缴费。

demo.title: Contactless mobile payment

frames.en: Phone wallet taps (NFC) or scans a QR code at the shop.
frames.zh: 手机钱包拍卡（NFC）或扫 QR code。

frames.en: The terminal sends the payment request over the Internet.
frames.zh: 终端经 Internet 发出付款要求。

frames.en: The platform moves money to the shop's account and both get a record.
frames.zh: 平台把钱转到商户户口，双方有纪录。

cards.en:
Analogy: the office comes to you through the Internet, like a TV show streaming into your living room.

Instant messaging, video conferencing, cloud collaboration and remote logon made Small Office/Home Office (SOHO) possible: staff access company files and work together online, so being in the office is no longer a must.

ProsCons
EmployersLower rent and operating costs (smaller office); hire talent anywhereRisk of data breaches due to insecure connections outside the office; harder to supervise
EmployeesSave commuting time; flexible hoursExtra cost of computer + Internet; blurred work-life boundary; less social contact

Exam wording: always say who (employer/employee) gets the pro or con.
cards.zh:
比喻：办公室经 Internet 来到你家，像串流节目送到客厅。

即时通讯、视像会议、云端协作、远程登入令 SOHO（小型／家居办公室）可行：员工经网络存取公司文件、合作，不必回公司。

好处坏处
雇主租金及营运成本低；可聘任何地方的人才办公室外连线不安全，可能数据外泄；难监督
员工省交通时间；时间弹性自付电脑和上网；工作生活界线模糊；少社交

考试写法：一定要写明是谁（雇主／员工）的好处或坏处。

ex.q: One advantage to an employer and one disadvantage to an employee of working from home.
ex.a:
1. Employer: smaller office → lower rent/operating cost.
2. Employee: must pay for a computer and Internet at home (or blurred work-life boundary).
ex.az:
1. 雇主：租金低。
2. 员工：自付设备及上网费。

ex.q: Which technologies make SOHO possible? Give three.
ex.a:
1. Video conferencing for meetings.
2. Cloud collaboration to co-edit files.
3. Remote logon / VPN to reach office computers and files. (Also IM.)
ex.az:
1. 视像会议。
2. 云端协作。
3. 远程登入／VPN。

ex.q: A student lists "saves commuting time" as an advantage to the employer. What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Commuting time is saved by the employee, not the employer.
2. For the employer write: lower rent/operating cost.
3. Marks are lost when the stakeholder is mixed up.
ex.az:
1. 省交通时间是员工的好处。
2. 雇主应写：租金成本低。
3. 搞错对象会失分。

cards.t: Smart living, government, mobility, people, environment
cards.tz: 智慧生活、政府、交通、教育、环境
cards.en:
Analogy: the government and city services become apps in your pocket.

AreaExamples
Smart Living / GovernmentHA Go (hospital bookings, records); My Library (renew/reserve); iAM Smart: one digital identity to log in to government services, fill forms, sign digitally
Smart MobilityFree-flow Tolling (pay tunnel tolls without stopping); smart parking meters (real-time vacancy, online pay); real-time arrival info; real-time adaptive traffic signals
Smart People (education)Remote learning by video conference; online multimedia resources; automatic marking
Smart EnvironmentStreet lights reacting to movement; bin fill-level sensors to plan routes; remote monitoring of electricity, water quality, air pollution

More examples: HKeMobility app gives real-time travel information; automated car parks move cars to spaces on mechanical lifts; smart recycling bins use fill-level sensors; smart meters show real-time electricity use; smart people includes real-time evaluation (automatic marking, instant analysis of learning progress). Free-flow tolling uses RFID, like Autotoll but with no administration fee.

Exam wording: for a scenario, list Internet services as search (database access), update records, store data, calculate.
cards.zh:
比喻：政府和城市服务变成口袋里的 app。

范畴例子
生活／政府HA Go；My Library；智方便 iAM Smart：一个数码身份登入政府服务、填表、数码签署
交通不停车缴费；智能咪表（实时空位、网上付款）；实时到站资讯；实时交通灯调节
教育视像遥距学习；网上多媒体资源；自动批改
环境感应街灯；垃圾桶满载感应器；遥距监测电力、水质、空气

更多例子：HKeMobility 提供实时交通资讯；自动泊车系统用机械升降台把车送到车位；智能回收桶用满溢感应器；智能电表显示实时用电；智慧市民包括实时评估（自动评分、即时分析学习进度）。不停车缴费系统用 RFID，类似快易通但不收行政费。

考试写法：情境题可写搜寻（存取数据库）、更新纪录、储存数据、计算。

ex.q: A library installs self-service kiosks connected to a server. Suggest three Internet services.
ex.a:
1. Search books (database access).
2. Update book availability (database update).
3. Store borrowing records (data storage).
4. Calculate overdue fines (computation). Any three.
ex.az:
1. 搜书。
2. 更新书本状态。
3. 储存借阅纪录。
4. 计罚款（任三项）。

ex.q: How does the Free-flow Tolling System improve traffic?
ex.a:
1. A tag in the car is read automatically at the toll point.
2. The toll is charged to the account online.
3. Cars don't stop at booths → less queuing and congestion (Smart Mobility).
ex.az:
1. 自动读车上标签。
2. 网上扣费。
3. 不用停车 → 少塞车。

ex.q: A student puts iAM Smart under Smart Mobility. Correct it.
ex.a:
1. iAM Smart is a digital identity for logging in to government online services.
2. So it belongs to Smart Government / Smart Living.
3. Smart Mobility is about transport (tolls, parking, traffic lights).
ex.az:
1. iAM Smart 是登入政府服务的数码身份。
2. 属 Smart Government／Living。
3. Mobility 是交通。

cards.en:
Analogy: email is like posting a letter: the address tells the post office (mail server) which building and which person.

Email (electronic mail) = messages sent through the Internet. It is cross-platform: you open your mailbox with any browser or app, on any device, and can mail anyone regardless of the email service provider (Gmail ↔ Outlook).

Address = username + @ + domain name of the mail server, e.g. tom@abcss.edu.hk. The username can be a person, a mailing list, an organisation or a role (info@).

Email vs instant messaging: more formal; cross-platform; larger attachments, not compressed; searchable record; recipient needs no special app.

Exam wording: "Email is a cross-platform communication method; users can send email to anyone regardless of the email service provider."
cards.zh:
比喻：email 像寄信：地址告诉邮局（mail server）哪座大厦、哪个人。

Email = 经 Internet 传送的讯息，跨平台：任何浏览器、app、装置都能开邮箱，不论服务供应商都能互相收发。

地址 = username + @ + domain name，如 tom@abcss.edu.hk；username 可以是个人、邮寄清单、机构或职位（info@）。

比 IM 好：较正式、跨平台、附件较大且不压缩、纪录易搜寻、收件人不用装特定 app。

考试写法：Email is a cross-platform communication method; users can send email to anyone regardless of the email service provider.

ex.q: Identify the parts of mary.chan@abcss.edu.hk.
ex.a:
1. Username: mary.chan (owner of mailbox).
2. @ separates the two parts.
3. Domain name: abcss.edu.hk (the organisation's mail server).
ex.az:
1. username = mary.chan。
2. @ 分隔。
3. domain = abcss.edu.hk。

ex.q: Give two reasons a company emails job offers instead of using WhatsApp.
ex.a:
1. Email is more formal and keeps a searchable record.
2. Cross-platform: the applicant needs no particular app; attachments (contract PDF) are not compressed.
ex.az:
1. 正式、有纪录。
2. 跨平台，附件不被压缩。

ex.q: A student says a Gmail user cannot email an Outlook user because they are different companies. Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Wrong.
2. Email is cross-platform: mail servers of different providers exchange messages through the Internet using standard protocols.
3. So Gmail ↔ Outlook works.
ex.az:
1. 错。
2. 不同供应商的 mail server 用标准协定互通。
3. 所以可收发。

demo.title: An email's journey

frames.en: Tom presses Send in his app.
frames.zh: Tom 在 app 按发送。

frames.en: His provider's mail server reads the domain after @.
frames.zh: 供应商 mail server 读 @ 后的 domain。

frames.en: It passes the message to the receiver's mail server, even if a different provider.
frames.zh: 经 Internet 交给收件人 mail server，即使供应商不同。

frames.en: Mary opens her mailbox from any browser or app.
frames.zh: Mary 用任何浏览器或 app 打开邮箱。

cards.en:
Analogy: To = the person you talk to; Cc = someone standing next to you listening; Bcc = someone hiding behind the curtain: they hear everything but nobody knows they are there.

FieldShown to others?Use
ToYes, in headerMain recipients who must take action
Cc (carbon copy)Yes, in headerCopy for information only
Bcc (blind carbon copy)No, hiddenCopy without others knowing; bulk mail, protects recipients' privacy

Who sees what: To and Cc people see the To + Cc lists. A Bcc person sees To + Cc + only their own address, never other Bcc addresses.

Exam wording: "Use Bcc when sending bulk email so that recipients' email addresses are not disclosed to each other (protect personal data)."
cards.zh:
比喻：To = 你对着说话的人；Cc = 站在旁边听的人；Bcc = 躲在帘后：听到一切，但没人知道他在。

栏别人看到？用途
To看到主要收件人，要跟进
Cc看到只供参考
Bcc隐藏不让人知道的副本；大量发信时保护私隐

谁看到什么：To／Cc 看到 To + Cc；Bcc 看到 To + Cc + 自己，看不到其他 Bcc。

考试写法：Use Bcc when sending bulk email so that recipients' email addresses are not disclosed to each other.

ex.q: Janice emails To: Patrick, Cc: George, Bcc: Mrs Lee. (a) What does she expect from Patrick? (b) Do Patrick and George know Mrs Lee got it?
ex.a:
1. (a) Patrick is in To → he should take action; George (Cc) is for information.
2. (b) No. Mrs Lee is in Bcc, so her address is hidden from the header.
ex.az:
1. Patrick 要跟进；George 只参考。
2. 不知道，Mrs Lee 在 Bcc。

ex.q: A club emails 200 members about a meeting. Which field should hold the members' addresses? Why?
ex.a:
1. Bcc (put the club's own address in To).
2. Each member cannot see the other 199 addresses.
3. This protects personal data and stops a mass Reply All.
ex.az:
1. 放 Bcc（To 放自己）。
2. 会员看不到其他地址。
3. 保护私隐，避免全部回覆。

ex.q: A teacher puts all 200 parents in Cc "so they get a copy". What is the problem?
ex.a:
1. Cc addresses appear in the header for everyone.
2. Every parent sees the other 199 email addresses → personal data leaked.
3. Correct: use Bcc for bulk mail.
ex.az:
1. Cc 地址人人看到。
2. 家长互相看到地址 → 泄露个人资料。
3. 应用 Bcc。

demo.title: What each person sees

frames.en: To: Patrick, Cc: George, Bcc: Mrs Lee.
frames.zh: To：Patrick，Cc：George，Bcc：Mrs Lee。

frames.en: Header shows To: Patrick, Cc: George. No Mrs Lee.
frames.zh: 看到 To：Patrick，Cc：George，没有 Mrs Lee。

frames.en: Same header as Patrick: he does not know about Mrs Lee.
frames.zh: 与 Patrick 相同，不知道 Mrs Lee。

frames.en: She sees To: Patrick, Cc: George and herself in Bcc. Other Bcc people would stay hidden.
frames.zh: 她看到 To、Cc 和自己的 Bcc；其他 Bcc 仍隐藏。

cards.en:
Analogy: Reply = whisper back to the speaker; Reply All = answer out loud to everyone who was visibly in the room; Forward = take the letter to someone new.

  • Reply: goes only to the original sender.
  • Reply All: goes to the sender and all To and Cc recipients. Bcc recipients are not included (their addresses were hidden).
  • Forward: sends to new recipients; attachments are forwarded by default. The forwarded text shows To and Cc only, so Bcc is not disclosed.

Email history is attached automatically. A Bcc person misses later replies: pro avoids extra emails; con they are left out of the discussion. If a Bcc person clicks Reply All, everyone learns they got it.

Exam wording: "Reply All sends to the sender and all recipients in the To and Cc fields; Bcc recipients are not included."
cards.zh:
比喻：Reply = 只回答说话的人；Reply All = 对房内看得见的所有人回答；Forward = 把信拿给新的人。

  • Reply：只回原寄件人。
  • Reply All：回寄件人及所有 To、Cc；不包括 Bcc。
  • Forward：给新收件人，附件预设一并转寄；只显示 To/Cc，Bcc 不曝光。

旧邮件内容自动附上。Bcc 收件人收不到之后的回覆：好处是少多余邮件；坏处是被排除于讨论外。Bcc 的人若按 Reply All，大家就知道他收过。

考试写法：Reply All sends to the sender and all recipients in the To and Cc fields; Bcc recipients are not included.

ex.q: Janice emails To: Patrick, Cc: George, Bcc: Mrs Lee. Patrick clicks Reply All. Who receives it?
ex.a:
1. Reply All = sender + To + Cc, minus the replier.
2. Sender: Janice. To: Patrick (himself, removed). Cc: George.
3. Result: Janice and George. Mrs Lee (Bcc) does not.
ex.az:
1. 寄件人 + To + Cc，减去自己。
2. 结果：Janice 和 George。
3. Mrs Lee 收不到。

ex.q: Patrick forwards the email to Kelvin. Does Kelvin get the attachment? Does he see Mrs Lee's address?
ex.a:
1. Yes, attachments are forwarded by default.
2. No, the forwarded message only shows To and Cc; Bcc stays hidden.
ex.az:
1. 会收到附件。
2. 看不到，Bcc 不显示。

ex.q: A student says: "Reply All also reaches Bcc recipients because they got the original." Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Wrong: the replier's client never knew the Bcc addresses (they were hidden from the header).
2. So Reply All only reaches the sender + To + Cc.
3. Bcc recipients are left out of later replies.
ex.az:
1. 错：Bcc 地址在 header 中隐藏，回覆者不知道。
2. 所以只到寄件人 + To + Cc。
3. Bcc 收不到后续回覆。

demo.title: Reply vs Reply All vs Forward (Patrick acts)

frames.en: Only Janice gets it.
frames.zh: 只有 Janice 收到。

frames.en: Janice and George (To + Cc). Mrs Lee is NOT included.
frames.zh: Janice 和 George；不包括 Mrs Lee。

frames.en: Kelvin gets the message plus attachment; Bcc not shown.
frames.zh: Kelvin 收到内容及附件；不显示 Bcc。

cards.en:
Analogy: attachment = putting the photo inside the envelope; inline = printing the photo on the letter itself; hyperlink = writing "the photo is in locker 42" so the envelope stays thin.

MethodFeaturesGood for
AttachmentFile travels with the email; takes mailbox space; size limit (e.g. 25 MB)Small files (documents)
Inline embeddingFile shown in the message body; mostly images; some clients block auto image loadingImages, posters
HyperlinkFile kept on cloud/hosting site; much larger limit; no mailbox spaceLarge files (videos), websites

Hyperlink cons: link becomes invalid if the file is removed; may need permission/Internet to open.

Exam wording: "The email only contains the URL, so it does not take up storage space in the mailbox."
cards.zh:
比喻：附件 = 相片放进信封；内置 = 把相片印在信纸上；超连结 = 写“相片在 42 号储物柜”，信封很薄。

方法特点适合
Attachment随邮件传；占邮箱空间；有大小限制（如 25 MB）小文件
Inline embedding显示于内文；多为图片；有些 client 不自动载入图片、海报
Hyperlink文件在云端；限制大得多；不占邮箱影片等大文件

连结缺点：文件被删除后连结失效；或要权限／网络。

考试写法：The email only contains the URL, so it does not take up storage space in the mailbox.

ex.q: Choose a method: (i) a 2 MB PDF form; (ii) a 1.5 GB video; (iii) an event poster readers should see immediately.
ex.a:
1. (i) Attachment: small, recipient keeps a copy.
2. (ii) Hyperlink: far above the ~25 MB email limit.
3. (iii) Inline embedding: image appears in the body.
ex.az:
1. 附件。
2. 超连结（超过约 25 MB 限制）。
3. 内置图片。

ex.q: Why does a poster sent as a hosting link take less mailbox space than an attachment?
ex.a:
1. With a link the image stays on the hosting site.
2. The email holds only the URL text (a few bytes).
3. An attachment puts the whole file into the email.
ex.az:
1. 图片留在寄存网站。
2. 邮件只含网址文字。
3. 附件把整个文件放进邮件。

ex.q: A student shares a cloud link to the class video, then deletes the file to free space. Classmates get an error. What went wrong?
ex.a:
1. A hyperlink only points to the file; it is not a copy.
2. Deleting the file makes the link invalid.
3. Keep the file in cloud storage (and set share permission) until everyone has it.
ex.az:
1. 连结只是指向文件，不是副本。
2. 删除后连结失效。
3. 应保留文件并设定分享权限。

cards.en:
Analogy: the provider is a security guard at the door who learns from you: each time you say "this one is junk" or "this one is fine", the guard gets better.

Spam = unwanted bulk email (ads, scams). Most is detected and blocked by the provider with AI, but some spam gets through and some good email is wrongly moved to the spam folder.

  • Mark as spam / not spam → improves detection accuracy.
  • Whitelist (safe senders: never treated as spam) and blacklist (blocked senders).
  • Don't auto-load images from untrusted senders: spammers count image downloads to find the open rate and confirm your address is active; images may also carry malware.

Exam wording: "Mark the email as spam to improve the accuracy of the spam filter"; "add the sender to the whitelist".
cards.zh:
比喻：供应商像门口的保安，会向你学习：每次你说“这是垃圾”或“这封没问题”，保安就更准。

Spam = 不想要的大量邮件（广告、诈骗）。大部分由供应商以 AI 侦测及阻挡，但会漏网，也会误判正常邮件。

  • Mark as spam / not spam → 提高准确度。
  • Whitelist（安全寄件人）及 blacklist（封锁）。
  • 不自动载入陌生寄件人的图片：spammer 用图片下载次数计 open rate，确认地址有效；图片亦可能藏恶意程式。

考试写法：Mark the email as spam to improve the accuracy of the spam filter; add the sender to the whitelist.

ex.q: Why might a client ask 'Display images below?' for mail from an unknown sender?
ex.a:
1. Loading a remote image sends a request to the sender's server.
2. The sender learns the email was opened (open rate) and the address is active → more spam.
3. The image could be malicious, so it is blocked until you trust the sender.
ex.az:
1. 载入图片会向寄件人伺服器发要求。
2. 对方知道你开信（open rate）→ 更多 spam。
3. 图片可能有害，所以先封锁。

ex.q: The school's notices keep landing in the spam folder. What should the student do?
ex.a:
1. Open the notice and click Not spam.
2. Add the school's address to the whitelist / contacts.
3. Future notices go to the inbox.
ex.az:
1. 按 Not spam。
2. 把学校地址加入 whitelist。
3. 以后会入收件匣。

ex.q: A user replies "unsubscribe me!" to every spam email. Why is this a mistake?
ex.a:
1. Replying proves the address is real and active.
2. The spammer can sell it or send more spam / phishing.
3. Correct: don't reply; mark as spam or blacklist the sender.
ex.az:
1. 回覆证明地址有效。
2. 对方会发更多 spam 或出售地址。
3. 应标记 spam 或封锁。

cards.en:
Analogy: remote logon is like a very long keyboard and mouse cable from your home to the school computer, plus a live video of its screen.

Remote logon (remote access) = remotely accessing a device from another device. Authorised users connect to, or even control, a far-away device (IT support, using a school PC from home).

  • Host = the computer being controlled; client = the computer you sit at.
  • Remote desktop software (AnyDesk, Chrome Remote Desktop, Microsoft Remote Desktop), usually cross-platform.
  • Secure software provides authentication, VPN and encryption.
  • Requirements: the same remote desktop software on both computers; the host is on and connected to the Internet.
  • Chrome Remote Desktop: host sets a PIN (6+ digits); for remote support a one-time access code valid for 5 minutes, and the host must approve.

Exam wording: "Only the screen image is sent to the client; the program runs on the host computer."
cards.zh:
比喻：远程登入就像从家里拉一条超长的键盘滑鼠线到学校电脑，再加它屏幕的直播。

远程登入（remote access）= 用一部设备远距离存取另一部设备，授权用户可连接甚至控制它（IT 支援、在家用学校电脑）。

  • Host = 被控制的电脑；client = 你面前的电脑。
  • Remote desktop software（AnyDesk、Chrome Remote Desktop），通常跨平台。
  • 安全软件要有 authentication、VPN、encryption。
  • 条件：两边装相同软件；host 开机并连网。
  • Chrome Remote Desktop：host 设 6 位以上 PIN；远程支援用5 分钟有效的一次性存取码，并需 host 批准。

考试写法：Only the screen image is sent to the client; the program runs on the host computer.

ex.q: John wants to use the school's 3D modelling software from home. What setup is needed?
ex.a:
1. Install the same remote desktop software on the school PC (host) and home PC (client).
2. Leave the school PC switched on and connected to the Internet.
3. Set up authentication (PIN / password) and log in from home.
ex.az:
1. 两部电脑装相同软件。
2. 学校电脑保持开机连网。
3. 设 PIN／密码后在家登入。

ex.q: An IT technician fixes a user's PC with Chrome Remote Desktop. Describe the steps.
ex.a:
1. User opens 'Remote support' and generates a one-time access code (valid 5 minutes).
2. User tells the code to the technician.
3. Technician enters it; user clicks to approve sharing.
4. Technician controls the PC; session ends when user stops sharing.
ex.az:
1. 用户产生 5 分钟一次性码。
2. 告诉技术员。
3. 技术员输入，用户批准。
4. 技术员控制电脑。

ex.q: A student says the home laptop needs a powerful GPU to run the school's 3D software by remote logon. Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Wrong: the software runs on the host (school PC).
2. The client only sends keyboard/mouse input and shows the screen image.
3. So a weak laptop is fine; network speed matters more.
ex.az:
1. 错：软件在 host 运行。
2. client 只传输入、显示画面。
3. 弱电脑也可，网速更重要。

demo.title: A remote logon session

frames.en: Client enters the host's PIN / access code; the connection is encrypted.
frames.zh: client 输入 PIN／存取码，连线加密。

frames.en: Your mouse clicks and key presses travel to the host.
frames.zh: 滑鼠键盘输入传到 host。

frames.en: The program runs on the school PC using its CPU/GPU and licence.
frames.zh: 程式在学校电脑运行，用它的 CPU/GPU 和授权。

frames.en: Only the screen image streams back to your laptop.
frames.zh: 只有画面传回你的电脑。

cards.t: Benefits and limitations of remote logon
cards.tz: 远程登入的好处与限制
cards.en:
Analogy: borrowing a friend's sports car by remote control: you get its power, but if the signal is weak the car lags, and someone could listen to the controls.

BenefitsLimitations
Use software licensed to a specific computer without extra subscriptionData breach may occur during transmission over the Internet
Run resource-intensive programs on a more powerful computerHigh latency (delay) if either side has a poor connection or runs out of RAM
Access files anytime anywhere; reach resources limited to the school's IP addressThe remote computer must stay on
IT team gives remote support

Security measures: encrypt data transmission; two-factor authentication (2FA) or one-time password.

Exam wording: "The program is executed on the remote computer, so the user can make use of its hardware and software licence."
cards.zh:
比喻：遥控借用朋友的跑车：有它的马力，但讯号弱会延迟，也可能被人偷听指令。

好处限制
用只授权给某部电脑的软件，不用另外订阅传输中可能数据外泄
在更强的电脑运行重型程式任何一方网络差或 RAM 不足 → 高延迟
随时存取文件；用只限学校 IP 的资源远端电脑要一直开着
IT 远程支援

保安：加密传输；2FA 或一次性密码。

考试写法：The program is executed on the remote computer, so the user can make use of its hardware and software licence.

ex.q: A user has high latency in a remote session. One cause and one security feature the software should have.
ex.a:
1. Cause: poor connection / low bandwidth on either side, or a computer out of RAM.
2. Security: encrypt transmitted data, or 2FA / one-time password.
ex.az:
1. 原因：网络差或 RAM 不足。
2. 保安：加密或 2FA。

ex.q: Why is remote logon useful for a student who needs software licensed only to school computers?
ex.a:
1. The licence is tied to the school PC.
2. By remote logon the program still runs on that PC.
3. So the student can use it from home without buying another licence.
ex.az:
1. 授权绑定学校电脑。
2. 远程登入时程式仍在该电脑运行。
3. 不用另买授权。

ex.q: A student says a VPN makes remote logon faster. What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. A VPN's job is security: it encrypts the connection (a private tunnel).
2. It usually adds a little delay, not speed.
3. Speed depends on bandwidth and the computers' resources.
ex.az:
1. VPN 用于保安（加密通道）。
2. 通常稍为变慢。
3. 速度取决于频宽及资源。

cards.en:
Analogy: email is a letter; online chat is a phone call in text: quick, short, back and forth.

Online chat enables private conversation with an individual or a group using text, audio, images, video, emoticons and stickers, anytime and anywhere.

  • Direct messages on social networking sites.
  • Instant messaging (IM) apps (WhatsApp, Signal, WeChat), with voice and video calls.
  • Online messaging service to reach customer service or online sellers.
Online chatEmail
Real-time, informalFormal, not instant
Both sides usually need the same appCross-platform
Media often compressedAttachments kept as original

Live chat support vs email: instant responses, customers get help without switching to other apps. vs phone: one officer can handle several chats at once; customers avoid long call-centre queues. Risk of IM apps: unencrypted metadata (sending time, recipients) can reveal social relationships and usage patterns.

Exam wording: "Online chat allows real-time communication with an individual or a group using multimedia."
cards.zh:
比喻：email 像信件；网上聊天像用文字打电话：快、短、来回。

网上聊天让人与个人或群组私下对话，可用文字、语音、图片、影片、表情、贴图，随时随地。

  • 社交网站私讯。
  • IM app（WhatsApp、Signal、微信），有语音／视像通话。
  • 客服网上讯息。
网上聊天Email
实时、随意正式、非即时
双方通常要同一 app跨平台
媒体常被压缩附件保持原档

Live chat 客服 vs 电邮：即时回应，客户不用转到其他 app。vs 电话：一位客服可同时处理多个对话；客户不用长时间排队。IM 的风险：未加密的 metadata（发送时间、收件人）可泄露社交关系和使用习惯。

考试写法：Online chat allows real-time communication with an individual or a group using multimedia.

ex.q: Give one advantage of email over IM for sending a job application.
ex.a:
1. Email is cross-platform: employer needs no particular app.
2. It is more formal and keeps a searchable record.
3. The CV attachment is not compressed.
ex.az:
1. 跨平台。
2. 正式、有纪录。
3. 附件不被压缩。

ex.q: A shop wants to answer customers' questions within seconds. Which service fits and why?
ex.a:
1. An online messaging (chat) service on its website/app.
2. It is real-time, so questions are answered at once.
3. Customers can send photos of the product problem.
ex.az:
1. 网上客服聊天。
2. 实时回答。
3. 可传相片。

ex.q: A student says IM is cross-platform because WhatsApp runs on iPhone and Android. Correct the idea.
ex.a:
1. Running on many devices ≠ cross-platform in the email sense.
2. A WhatsApp user cannot message a WeChat user: both sides need the same app.
3. Email works between any providers → that is cross-platform.
ex.az:
1. 多装置可用不等于跨平台。
2. WhatsApp 不能传给微信，双方要同一 app。
3. Email 不同供应商互通才是跨平台。

cards.en:
Analogy: a forum is a classroom notice board sorted by subject; a social networking site is the playground where friends share what they did.

Discussion forums (message boards): online platforms to ask and answer questions or share content on a certain topic (Reddit, Quora, Stack Exchange where users upvote useful answers, Uwants, Baby Kingdom). Forums in learning platforms increase interaction in online teaching.

Social Networking Sites (SNS) / social media: let people stay connected by sharing experiences and ideas in text, images, audio, video; keep in touch and meet people with similar interests. Blogs grew out of online diaries.

Risks of SNS: personal information overexposed, fake news, phishing, cyberbullying.

Exam wording: forum = topic-based Q&A; SNS = stay connected by sharing experiences.
cards.zh:
比喻：讨论区像按科目分类的壁报板；社交网站像操场，朋友分享自己做过什么。

讨论区：按主题发问、回答、分享（Reddit、Quora、Stack Exchange 可 upvote、Uwants、BK）；学习平台讨论区增加网上教学互动。

SNS 社交网站：以文字、图片、影音分享经验和想法、保持联系，结识兴趣相近的人；Blog 由网上日记演变。

风险：个人资料过度曝光、假消息、钓鱼、网络欺凌。

考试写法：forum = 按主题问答；SNS = 分享经验保持联系。

ex.q: Why post a programming question on Stack Exchange rather than social media?
ex.a:
1. Forums are organised by topic, so experts in that topic reply.
2. Good answers are upvoted → reliable ones are easy to spot.
3. The Q&A stays searchable for others later.
ex.az:
1. 按主题，有专家回答。
2. 好答案被 upvote。
3. 之后可搜寻。

ex.q: A teacher adds a forum to the online course. State one benefit.
ex.a:
1. Students post questions anytime and classmates/teacher reply.
2. This increases interaction in online teaching.
3. Answers are kept for everyone to read.
ex.az:
1. 随时发问，同学老师回答。
2. 增加互动。
3. 答案保留供人参考。

ex.q: A student posts holiday photos with his home address and school uniform on a public SNS profile "because only friends follow me". What's the mistake?
ex.a:
1. Public posts can be seen by strangers, not only followers.
2. Address + uniform reveal personal information → stalking, phishing risks.
3. Correct: set the account private and don't share identifying details.
ex.az:
1. 公开帖子陌生人也看到。
2. 地址和校服泄露个人资料。
3. 应设为私人，不分享可识别资料。

cards.t: Blogs, vlogs and how SNS absorbed them
cards.tz: 博客、Vlog 与 SNS 的整合
cards.en:
Plain idea: a blog is someone's online diary; a forum is a group discussion; an SNS mixes both with friends and comments.

  • Blog: grew from online diaries; shares personal experiences, ideas and reviews. Only the owner can start topics. Vlog = video blog.
  • Discussion forum / message board: anyone can ask and answer questions on a subject (Reddit, Quora, Uwants, Baby Kingdom).
  • SNS: share experiences in text, images, audio, video; keep in touch and meet people with similar interests; has social interaction features such as comments.

Many bloggers and forum users moved to SNS because SNS integrated posts and community discussions. Xanga and Yahoo! Blog closed in 2014. But blogs and forums still exist (Blogger, Reddit, Quora): they are more flexible for multimedia and more readable for long articles or threads, so SNS users often link to them.

Is every blog an SNS? Not exactly: a site counts as SNS when it allows social interaction such as comments; otherwise it is just a website giving out information.

Exam wording: In a blog only the owner can initiate topics, while in a discussion forum any user can start a discussion on a subject.
cards.zh:
简单理解：博客是个人网上日记；论坛是群组讨论；SNS 把两者结合，加上朋友和留言。

  • Blog（博客）：源自网上日记，分享个人经历、想法、评论。只有博主可开话题。Vlog = 影片博客。
  • 讨论区／留言板：任何人都可就某主题发问和回答（Reddit、Quora、Uwants、Baby Kingdom）。
  • SNS：以文字、图片、声音、影片分享经历；保持联系、认识志趣相投的人；有留言等社交互动功能。

很多博主和论坛用户转用 SNS，因为 SNS 整合了发文和社群讨论。Xanga、Yahoo! Blog 于 2014 年关闭。但博客和论坛仍存在（Blogger、Reddit、Quora）：加插多媒体更灵活、长文或话题更易读，所以 SNS 用户常转介到这些地方。

所有博客都是 SNS 吗？不一定：要有留言等社交互动才算 SNS，否则只是发布资讯的网站。

考试写法：In a blog only the owner can initiate topics, while in a discussion forum any user can start a discussion on a subject.

ex.q: Ben wants to ask strangers which graphing calculator suits DSE Maths and compare many answers. Blog, forum or SNS?
ex.a:
1. A discussion forum.
2. Anyone can answer a topic-based question, so he gets many views (collective intelligence), often anonymously.
ex.az:
1. 讨论区。
2. 任何人都可回答，集思广益。

ex.q: Why do some SNS users still post a link to their blog for a long travel article?
ex.a:
1. Blogs are more readable for long articles.
2. They are more flexible for adding multimedia along with text.
ex.az:
1. 博客长文较易读。
2. 加插多媒体更灵活。

ex.q: A student says: "In a blog, any visitor can start a new topic." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: that describes a forum.
2. In a blog, only the owner can initiate topics; visitors may only comment.
ex.az:
1. 错误：那是论坛。
2. 博客只有博主可开话题。

cards.en:
Analogy: choosing how to send a file is like choosing a courier: a bike (IM) is fast but only carries small, squashed parcels; a truck (cloud) carries big boxes; an armoured van (VPN) is the safest.

Three factors: file size, file format, security. End-to-end encryption = only sender and receiver can read it. Peer-to-peer (P2P) = computers send files directly to each other, no central server.

MethodFormatSize limitEncryption
Instant messagingAuto image/video compressionSmallUsually end-to-end
EmailNo restrictionSmallOnly if both providers support it
Cloud storageNo restrictionLargeSome; relatively low
Network drive over VPNNo restrictionNone if enough storageYes
P2P file sharingNo restrictionNone if enough storageNo

Exam wording: justify with the factor: "large file size → cloud storage; confidential → network drive over VPN".
cards.zh:
比喻：选传输方法像选速递：单车（IM）快但只送小件、会压扁；货车（云端）送大箱；运钞车（VPN）最安全。

三因素：文件大小、格式、保安。端对端加密 = 只有收发双方能读。P2P = 电脑直接互传，没有中央伺服器。

方法格式大小限制加密
IM自动压缩图片影片小通常端对端
Email不限小双方供应商支援才有
云端不限大部分；较低
VPN 网络硬碟不限够空间就无限有
P2P不限够空间就无限无

考试写法：用因素解释：大文件 → cloud；机密 → VPN network drive。

ex.q: A friend sent a holiday vlog by IM but the quality is low. Why? What should be used instead?
ex.a:
1. IM apps automatically compress video to save data.
2. Use a cloud storage link (or network drive): keeps the original file, allows large size.
ex.az:
1. IM 自动压缩影片。
2. 改用云端连结，保持原画质。

ex.q: A company sends confidential 5 GB design files between branches. Best method?
ex.a:
1. Network drive over VPN.
2. No size limit if storage is enough (5 GB is fine).
3. Data is encrypted through the VPN → secure.
ex.az:
1. VPN 网络硬碟。
2. 无大小限制。
3. 有加密，安全。

ex.q: A student chooses P2P sharing for exam papers "because it has no size limit, so it's the best". What is missed?
ex.a:
1. Only the size factor was checked.
2. P2P has no encryption → confidential papers could leak.
3. Must consider all three factors; choose a VPN network drive.
ex.az:
1. 只考虑了大小。
2. P2P 不加密，会泄露。
3. 要考虑三因素，应用 VPN。

cards.t: File transfer methods: pros, cons and limits
cards.tz: 文件传送方法：优缺点与限制
cards.en:
Plain idea: pick by file size, file format and security.

MethodAdvantagesDisadvantages
Messaging app (WhatsApp ~16 MB media)Auto compression saves data and time; usually end-to-end encryptedLower image/video quality; may need software; small size limit
Email (Gmail 25 MB)Uncompressed files, no quality loss; cross-platformSmall size limit; extra fee for more storage
Cloud storage (OneDrive 250 GB, Google Drive 750 GB per file)Large size limit; no quality loss; auto-sync; online preview; file versioning; usually cross-platformExtra fee for storage; offline only after download
Network drive over VPNNo size/format limit; lower security risk; less cloud breach risk; centralised managementNeeds VPN and network setup; hard to trace uploaders and changes
P2P file sharing (BitTorrent)Fast when there are many peers; still works if a central server is downMalware may be packaged with the torrent; low security

FTP transfers files between a computer and a server; SFTP adds encryption and authentication. Most browsers no longer support FTP, so an FTP client (e.g. WinSCP) is needed.

Cloud sharing risk: "Anyone with the link can view" → if the link leaks, anyone can see the files without authentication. Providers should use 2FA and encryption.

Exam wording: Cloud storage supports large files without compression and auto-sync, but files are only available offline after download.
cards.zh:
简单理解：按文件大小、格式、保安选择。

方法优点缺点
即时通讯 app（WhatsApp 媒体约 16 MB）自动压缩，省数据和时间；通常端对端加密图片／影片质素下降；或要装软件；上限小
电邮（Gmail 25 MB）可传未压缩文件，不失真；跨平台上限小；加储存要付费
云端储存（OneDrive 250 GB、Google Drive 750 GB）上限大；不失真；自动同步；网上预览；文件版本；通常跨平台加储存要付费；下载后才可离线使用
经 VPN 的网络磁碟无大小／格式限制；保安风险较低；减少云端外泄；集中管理要设定 VPN 及网络；难追踪上传者和改动
P2P 分享（BitTorrent）peer 多时下载快；中央服务器失灵仍可下载种子可能夹带恶意软件；保安低

FTP 在电脑与服务器之间传文件；SFTP 加入加密及认证。大部分浏览器已不支援 FTP，要用 FTP 客户端（如 WinSCP）。

云端分享风险：「任何知道连结的人都可查看」→ 连结外泄就无需认证都可看。供应商应用 2FA 及加密。

考试写法：Cloud storage supports large files without compression and auto-sync, but files are only available offline after download.

ex.q: A 2 GB high-resolution video must reach a client without losing quality. Which method suits best, and why not email or IM?
ex.a:
1. Cloud storage (share a link).
2. Large size limit and no compression.
3. Email limit is about 25 MB; IM compresses video and has a small limit.
ex.az:
1. 云端储存。
2. 上限大、不压缩。
3. 电邮约 25 MB；IM 会压缩。

ex.q: Give two advantages of turning on auto-sync for a cloud photo service.
ex.a:
1. Photos are safe if the phone is lost or damaged (no data loss).
2. Photos can be accessed from any device and shared at once without waiting to upload.
ex.az:
1. 手机遗失或损坏也不会失去相片。
2. 任何设备都可存取，可即时分享。

ex.q: A student says: "FTP and SFTP are the same; SFTP is just faster." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: the difference is security.
2. SFTP transfers files with encryption and authentication; FTP does not encrypt.
ex.az:
1. 错误：分别在保安。
2. SFTP 有加密及认证。

cards.en:
Analogy: a search engine is a librarian who reads every book in advance and writes an index card for each word, so when you ask, they can point to the best books in a second.

You can find information on websites, social media, forums, or most simply with a search engine (Google, Bing, Yahoo!).

  1. A crawler (program) visits web pages by following links.
  2. Words on pages are stored in an index.
  3. When you type a keyword, the engine looks it up in the index.
  4. Matching pages are ranked and shown. Results differ among engines but the idea is the same.

SEO (Search Engine Optimisation) = improving website traffic by increasing its ranking and visibility in search results (relevant keywords, good content, fast loading, links from other sites). Important for digital marketing: users rarely look past page 1.

Top results are not necessarily the most reliable: some are ads or just well optimised.

Exam wording: "SEO is the process of improving website traffic by increasing the rankings and visibility in search results."
cards.zh:
比喻：搜寻引擎像图书馆员：预先读完所有书，为每个字写索引卡，你一问就能指出最好的书。

找资讯可用网站、社交媒体、讨论区，最简单是搜寻引擎。

  1. Crawler（爬虫程式）沿连结浏览网页。
  2. 网页的字存入 index（索引）。
  3. 输入关键字时在索引中查找。
  4. 把相关网页排序显示。不同引擎结果不同，原理一样。

SEO = 提高网站在搜寻结果的排名和能见度，增加流量（合适关键字、好内容、快载入、其他网站连入）。用户少看第一页以后，故对数码营销重要。

排前的结果不一定最可靠：可能是广告或做了 SEO。

考试写法：SEO is the process of improving website traffic by increasing the rankings and visibility in search results.

ex.q: A bakery's website is on page 5 of results. What should it do and why?
ex.a:
1. Carry out SEO: relevant keywords, useful content, fast loading, links from other sites.
2. Its ranking rises toward page 1.
3. Most users only click page-1 results → more traffic/customers.
ex.az:
1. 做 SEO。
2. 排名上升。
3. 用户多只看第一页 → 更多流量。

ex.q: Describe what happens between typing a keyword and seeing results.
ex.a:
1. The engine does not search the live web; it looks up its index built earlier by crawlers.
2. It finds pages containing the keyword.
3. It ranks them (relevance, quality, etc.) and displays the list.
ex.az:
1. 查已建立的索引，不是即时搜全网。
2. 找出含关键字的网页。
3. 排序后显示。

ex.q: A student cites the first Google result as the most reliable source "because it ranks highest". What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Ranking reflects SEO and relevance, and top items may be ads.
2. High rank ≠ accurate or reliable.
3. Check the author, date, and cross-check with other sources.
ex.az:
1. 排名受 SEO 影响，前列可能是广告。
2. 排名高不等于可靠。
3. 要查作者、日期并交叉核对。

demo.title: How a search engine answers you

frames.en: Crawlers follow links and visit pages ahead of time.
frames.zh: 爬虫预先沿连结浏览网页。

frames.en: Words and their pages are saved in the index.
frames.zh: 字词和对应网页存入索引。

frames.en: You type keywords; the engine looks them up in the index.
frames.zh: 你输入关键字，引擎查索引。

frames.en: Matching pages are ranked; SEO affects this order.
frames.zh: 相关网页排序；SEO 影响次序。

cards.t: Four steps of information search; paid vs organic results
cards.tz: 搜寻资讯四步骤；付费与自然结果
cards.en:
Plain idea: know what you need before you type.

  1. Define your needs for information: What do you want to know? What do you already know? What is the information used for?
  2. Decide where to search: a specific site (dictionary, SNS, forum, shopping site, Hong Kong Observatory, census) or a search engine / database.
  3. Develop a search strategy: keywords, source types, Boolean logic.
  4. Refine your search.

Search engine results page:

  • Paid search results: sponsors and advertisements, usually at the top.
  • Organic search results: ranked by the engine's algorithm by relevance (matching keywords with page titles and content).

Search engines are useful when you do not know where to find information. Popular ones: Google, Yahoo!, DuckDuckGo, Bing.

Exam wording: Organic results are ranked by the search algorithm according to relevance, while paid results are advertisements from sponsors.
cards.zh:
简单理解：输入关键字前，先清楚自己需要什么。

  1. 界定资讯需要：想知道什么？已知道什么？资讯用来做什么？
  2. 决定在哪里搜寻：特定网站（字典、SNS、论坛、购物网站、天文台、人口普查）或搜寻器／数据库。
  3. 制定搜寻策略：关键字、来源类型、布尔逻辑。
  4. 改进搜寻。

搜寻结果页：

  • 付费结果（paid）：赞助商及广告，通常在最上面。
  • 自然结果（organic）：由搜寻器演算法按相关度排名（把关键字与网页标题、内容配对）。

当你不知道去哪里找时，搜寻器最有用。常见：Google、Yahoo!、DuckDuckGo、Bing。

考试写法：Organic results are ranked by the search algorithm according to relevance, while paid results are advertisements from sponsors.

ex.q: Chris wants tomorrow's weather. Where should he search, and why?
ex.a:
1. The Hong Kong Observatory website/app.
2. It is the official, credible and up-to-date source, so no general search is needed.
ex.az:
1. 天文台。
2. 官方、可信、最新。

ex.q: Why should a student not assume the first search result is the best?
ex.a:
1. The top results may be paid advertisements.
2. Organic ranking is about relevance, not reliability; the information still needs evaluation.
ex.az:
1. 最上面可能是付费广告。
2. 排名看相关度，不等于可靠。

ex.q: A student starts by typing random words before knowing what is needed. What step is missing?
ex.a:
1. Mistake: skipped step 1.
2. First define the need for information (what to know, what is known, what it is for), then decide where to search.
ex.az:
1. 错误：跳过第一步。
2. 先界定资讯需要，再决定去哪里找。

cards.en:
Analogy: a search engine is like asking a huge crowd in the street: fast, lots of answers, but anyone can shout anything. A database is like a school library's reference shelf: fewer items, but each one was checked before it was put there.

Search engine = a website that collects (crawls) web pages, builds an index and lists matching pages for your keywords (e.g. Google, Bing). Database here = an organised online collection of published material, e.g. journal or newspaper databases that schools and libraries subscribe to.

Search engineDatabase
Content can change anytimePublished content that does not change
Contributed by any Internet userEvaluated for accuracy by publishers
Usually freeOften needs subscription / login
Huge range, mixed qualityFocused, organised by author, date, subject

Digital libraries/databases vs traditional libraries: access anywhere, anytime; faster keyword searching. Both can be reliable.

Book table extras: search engine content is unstructured, can change anytime, contributed by any Internet user, free (with sponsors/ads). Database content is organised and structured, published and does not change, evaluated for accuracy by publishers, contributed by subject experts, subscription-based, usually no ads. Database examples: ScienceDirect, JSTOR, WiseNews, Statista.

Exam wording: Databases contain published content evaluated for accuracy by publishers, so they are a more reliable source for academic research. Search engine results can be contributed by any Internet user and may change at any time.
cards.zh:
比喻：搜寻引擎像在街上问一大群人：快、答案多，但谁都可以乱说。数据库像学校图书馆的参考书架：东西少一点，但每样都先经过检查。

Search engine 搜寻引擎：收集（crawl）网页、建立索引（index），按关键字列出相关网页。Database 数据库：这里指学校／图书馆订阅的期刊、报章等已出版资料的网上集合。

  • 搜寻引擎：内容随时改变、任何人都可贡献、多数免费、质素参差
  • 数据库：已出版、内容不变、经出版者审核准确性、通常要订阅／登入、按作者日期主题整理

数码图书馆好处：随时随地存取、关键字搜寻更快。

Exam wording：Databases contain published content evaluated for accuracy by publishers, so they are a more reliable source for academic research.

课本表格补充：搜寻器内容非结构化、随时改变、任何人都可贡献、免费（有赞助及广告）。数据库内容有组织、有结构、已出版不变、由出版商核实准确性、由专家撰写、需订阅、通常无广告。数据库例子：ScienceDirect、JSTOR、WiseNews、Statista。

ex.q: A student writing a Biology project chooses between search-engine results and the school's journal database. Recommend one and explain.
ex.a:
1. Recommend the journal database.
2. Its articles are published and evaluated for accuracy by publishers.
3. Search results can be written by any Internet user and can change at any time.
4. So the database is more reliable/credible for academic work.
ex.az:
1. 选期刊数据库。
2. 内容已出版并经出版者审核准确性。
3. 搜寻结果任何人都可写、随时改变。
4. 所以学术研究用数据库较可靠。

ex.q: Give two advantages of an online newspaper database over the printed newspapers kept in a traditional library.
ex.a:
1. It can be accessed anywhere and anytime with an Internet connection (and login).
2. Searching is faster: type keywords and filter by date/author instead of flipping pages.
ex.az:
1. 有网络就随时随地存取。
2. 用关键字和日期筛选，比翻报纸快。

ex.q: Tom says: 'The database costs money, so it must be worse than Google, which is free.' Is he right?
ex.a:
1. No. Price does not decide reliability.
2. The subscription pays for publishers who check and organise the content.
3. Free search results have mixed quality because anyone can publish.
Correct idea: for academic research the paid database is usually more reliable.
ex.az:
1. 错。价钱不代表可靠性。
2. 订阅费用于出版者审核和整理内容。
3. 免费搜寻结果质素参差。
正确：学术研究用数据库通常更可靠。

demo.title: How a search engine finds pages vs how a database is filled

frames.en: A program (crawler) visits web pages and follows links. Any page anyone publishes can be collected.
frames.zh: 爬虫程式浏览网页并跟随连结，任何人发布的网页都可能被收集。

frames.en: The search engine stores the words of each page in an index, like the index at the back of a book.
frames.zh: 搜寻引擎把网页字词存入索引，像书后的索引。

frames.en: You type keywords. The engine looks them up in the index and ranks matching pages. Quality is mixed: no one checked them.
frames.zh: 你输入关键字，引擎查索引并排序结果。质素参差，没人审核。

frames.en: In a journal database, publishers evaluate each article for accuracy before adding it, and the content does not change.
frames.zh: 期刊数据库：出版者先审核准确性才加入，内容不变。

cards.en:
Analogy: searching is like fishing with a net. A big net (vague words) catches everything, including rubbish. A smaller, well-placed net (good keywords + filters) catches what you want.

Four steps:

  1. Choose keywords – one idea can be said in different words, so try synonyms or related keywords (e.g. 'global warming' / 'climate change'). More specific keywords → fewer, more relevant results.
  2. Choose source types – All, Images, Videos, News, Books. Filters: Images – size, colour, type, publish date, usage rights (e.g. Creative Commons = licences saying how others may reuse a work); Videos – duration, publish date, quality, closed captions, source.
  3. Use Boolean logic – operators such as -, OR, "", site: to include or exclude words (next card).
  4. Refine your search – tools such as time range, region, site; review results and change keywords.

Private-search engines (e.g. DuckDuckGo) do not track users, but your browser or account can still link data to you.

Exam wording: Choose keywords (use synonyms / more specific keywords) → choose source type → use Boolean operators → refine the search (e.g. time range, usage rights filter).
cards.zh:
比喻：搜寻像用网捕鱼：网太大（字太笼统）连垃圾都捞上来；网放对位置（好关键字＋筛选）才捞到想要的。

  1. 选关键字：同一意思可有不同说法，试同义词／相关词；字愈具体，结果愈少愈准。
  2. 选来源类型：全部、图片、影片、新闻、书籍。图片筛选：尺寸、颜色、类型、日期、使用权限 usage rights（如 Creative Commons 授权）；影片：长度、日期、画质、字幕、来源。
  3. 用 Boolean 逻辑：-、OR、""、site:。
  4. 收窄搜寻：时间范围、地区、网站；检查结果再改关键字。

私隐搜寻引擎（DuckDuckGo）不追踪用户，但浏览器／帐户仍可能连结数据。

Exam wording：Choose keywords → choose source type → use Boolean operators → refine the search.

ex.q: Eva needs a free-to-use photo of a red panda for her poster. Describe how to search.
ex.a:
1. Keyword: 'red panda'.
2. Source type: Images.
3. Filter usage rights → Creative Commons licences; size → Large.
4. Open the source page and check the licence terms (e.g. need to credit the author).
ex.az:
1. 关键字 red panda。
2. 选图片。
3. 使用权限选 Creative Commons，尺寸选大。
4. 到原网页确认授权条款。

ex.q: Searching 'phone' gives 3 billion results. Suggest two ways to get more useful results for a project on phone addiction among teenagers.
ex.a:
1. Use more specific keywords: 'smartphone addiction teenagers'.
2. Try synonyms: 'mobile phone overuse adolescents'.
3. Refine: time range 'past year', region Hong Kong, or News/Books source type.
ex.az:
1. 用更具体关键字 smartphone addiction teenagers。
2. 试同义词。
3. 设时间范围、地区或来源类型。

ex.q: Ben thinks: 'Using more keywords always gives MORE results.' Correct him.
ex.a:
1. Wrong. Each extra keyword normally must also match, so results become fewer and more relevant.
2. Only OR widens a search.
Correct: more specific keywords → fewer, more relevant results.
ex.az:
1. 错。多加关键字通常结果更少更准。
2. 只有 OR 会令结果变多。

demo.title: Narrowing a search step by step

frames.en: panda → millions of pages (giant panda, red panda, software, brands…).
frames.zh: panda → 数百万结果，很杂。

frames.en: red panda → only the animal you want.
frames.zh: red panda → 只剩想要的动物。

frames.en: Click Images → only pictures.
frames.zh: 选图片。

frames.en: Tools → Usage rights → Creative Commons licences → only images you may reuse.
frames.zh: 工具 → 使用权限 → Creative Commons。

frames.en: Open the source page and read the licence before using the photo.
frames.zh: 打开原网页确认授权。

cards.en:
Analogy: operators are like instructions to a librarian: "not this", "either of these", "exactly these words", "only from that shelf".

TechniqueOperatorExampleResults
Exclude results- in front of the word (no space after -)apple -fruitfewer
Either keywordOR (capital letters) between termsmandarin orange OR tangerinemore
Exact phrasephrase inside "quotation marks""artificial intelligence"fewer
One website/domainsite: in front of the site (no space)site:gov.hkfewer

They can be combined: "smart city" site:gov.hk -tender.

Exam wording: Use "-" to exclude a keyword; use OR to include either term (widens results); use quotation marks for an exact match; use site: to search a specific website or domain.
cards.zh:
比喻：运算子像对图书馆员下指令：「不要这个」「这两个都可」「一字不差」「只在那个书架找」。

  • -：排除（apple -fruit），- 后不留空格，结果变少
  • OR（大写）：任一字词（mandarin orange OR tangerine），结果变多
  • ""：完全相符的词组，结果变少
  • site:：只搜指定网站或域名（site:gov.hk），结果变少

可组合："smart city" site:gov.hk -tender。

Exam wording：Use "-" to exclude; OR to include either term; quotation marks for an exact match; site: for a specific website or domain.

ex.q: Write a query to find pages about the iPhone on Hong Kong education sites only, excluding the word 'repair'.
ex.a:
1. Keyword: iPhone.
2. Limit to HK education domain: site:edu.hk.
3. Exclude: -repair.
Answer: iPhone site:edu.hk -repair
ex.az: iPhone site:edu.hk -repair

ex.q: Rank these by number of results (most first): (A) jaguar (B) jaguar -car (C) jaguar OR leopard (D) "jaguar speed" -car
ex.a:
1. OR adds pages with either word → C has the most.
2. A is the plain keyword.
3. B removes car pages → fewer than A.
4. D needs an exact phrase AND removes car → fewest.
Order: C > A > B > D.
ex.az: C（OR 最多）> A > B（排除 car）> D（词组＋排除，最少）。

ex.q: Kelly types site: gov.hk - typhoon to search government pages but excluding typhoon. Find the mistakes.
ex.a:
1. There must be no space after site: → site:gov.hk.
2. There must be no space between - and the word → -typhoon.
3. With spaces the symbols are treated as normal text.
Correct: site:gov.hk -typhoon
ex.az: site: 和 - 后面都不可有空格。正确：site:gov.hk -typhoon

demo.title: What each operator does to the results

frames.en: apple → pages about the fruit AND the company.
frames.zh: apple：水果和公司都有。

frames.en: apple -fruit → pages containing 'fruit' are removed.
frames.zh: apple -fruit：含 fruit 的网页被移除。

frames.en: tangerine OR "mandarin orange" → pages with either term, so MORE results.
frames.zh: OR：任一字词都算，结果更多。

frames.en: "smart city" → the two words must appear together in this order.
frames.zh: ""：两个字必须连在一起。

frames.en: "smart city" site:gov.hk → only pages on gov.hk domains.
frames.zh: site:：只限 gov.hk。

cards.en:
Analogy: before you trust a rumour from a classmate, you ask: do others say the same? who said it first? is it old news? Do the same with web pages.

Anyone with an Internet connection can access and publish information, and there is little quality control, so some information is inaccurate, out of date or incomplete. Check three things:

CriterionQuestionHow to check
Reliability (can it be trusted?)Same as other sources? Sources cited?Verify with other sources; check for broken links
Credibility (is the writer qualified?)Who wrote it?Check the domain (.gov, .edu, .org); search for information on the author
Timeliness (is it up to date?)When was it published/updated?Check the publish date; how often it is updated

Tools: reverse image search (find where a photo first appeared), fact-check labels.

Exam wording: Evaluate the reliability, credibility and timeliness of the information: verify with other sources, check the domain and the author, and check the publish date.
cards.zh:
比喻：听到同学说的传闻，你会问：别人也这样说吗？谁先说的？是旧闻吗？对网页也要这样做。

任何有网络的人都可发布资讯，缺乏质素控制，所以可能不准、过时、不完整。检查三方面：

  • Reliability 可靠性：与其他来源一致？有注明出处？→ 与其他来源核对、查失效连结
  • Credibility 可信性：作者有资格吗？→ 查域名（.gov/.edu/.org）、查作者背景
  • Timeliness 时效性：够新吗？→ 查发布日期、更新频率

工具：以图搜图、事实查核标签。

Exam wording：Evaluate reliability, credibility and timeliness: verify with other sources, check the domain and the author, check the publish date.

ex.q: A 2010 web page says the Zoological and Botanical Gardens have 'over 500 species of plants'. What should Eva do before using it?
ex.a:
1. Criterion: timeliness – the data is from 2010, it may be out of date.
2. Check the official site (a .gov.hk page) for the latest figure.
3. Compare with other credible sources (reliability).
ex.az:
1. 时效性：2010 年资料可能过时。
2. 到 .gov.hk 官方网站查最新数字。
3. 与其他可信来源比较。

ex.q: A health tip comes from a blog with no author name and no references. Which criteria are weak and how can you check?
ex.a:
1. Credibility weak: unknown author → search for the author; prefer .gov/.edu/.org sites such as the Department of Health.
2. Reliability weak: no sources cited → verify the tip with other trusted sources.
ex.az:
1. 可信性弱：作者不明 → 查作者，改用政府／大学网站。
2. 可靠性弱：无出处 → 用其他来源核实。

ex.q: Leo says: 'The site ends in .com and looks professional, so it is credible.' Comment.
ex.a:
1. A nice design does not prove anything; anyone can build a professional-looking site.
2. .com can be registered by anyone.
3. Correct way: check who the author/organisation is and verify the content with other sources.
ex.az:
1. 设计漂亮不代表可信，.com 任何人都可注册。
2. 应查作者／机构并与其他来源核对。

demo.title: Checking one web page in three moves

frames.en: Open two or three other sources. Do they give the same facts? Are sources cited? Any broken links?
frames.zh: 打开其他来源：资料一致吗？有出处吗？连结有效吗？

frames.en: Look at the domain (.gov.hk? .edu?) and search the author's name. Is he/she an expert in this field?
frames.zh: 看域名，搜寻作者背景。

frames.en: Find the publish/update date. Is it new enough for your purpose?
frames.zh: 找发布／更新日期，够新吗？

frames.en: Only use or share the information if it passes all three checks.
frames.zh: 三项都合格才使用或转发。

cards.t: Fake news, content farms and private browsing
cards.tz: 假新闻、内容农场与私密浏览
cards.en:
Plain idea: anyone can publish online with little quality control, so check before you share.

  • Social impacts of fake news: unnecessary panic (e.g. 2011 salt panic buying), reputational damage, monetary loss (phishing messages with links to fake Hongkong Post sites), distrust in media.
  • Content farm: a website that raises its hit rate by publishing lots of low-quality content with catchy headlines ("Lose 10 kg in a week"). Check the domain and compare with credible sources.
  • Fact-check images: use reverse image search to find the original source; some images show a "Fact Check" label.
  • Suspicious links: the displayed text may point to a fake site; check the real domain (e.g. hongkongpost.hk) or call the organisation.

Private browsing is not private: it only stops the local browser saving history, cookies and entered data. It does not hide your activity or IP address from the search engine, which can still link it to your account.

Exam wording: Before spreading information, verify it with the official website or other credible sources, because false information may lead others to make wrong decisions.
cards.zh:
简单理解：任何人都可在网上发布，缺乏质素控制，所以分享前要查证。

  • 假新闻的社会影响：无谓恐慌（如 2011 年抢购盐）、名誉受损、金钱损失（附假香港邮政网站连结的诈骗讯息）、对传媒失去信任。
  • 内容农场：用大量低质素、标题吸引的内容（「一星期减 10 公斤」）提高点击率的网站。要检查域名并与可信来源比较。
  • 查证图片：用以图搜图（reverse image search）找原始来源；部分图片有「Fact Check」标签。
  • 可疑连结：显示的文字可能连到假网站；检查真正域名（如 hongkongpost.hk）或致电该机构。

私密浏览并不私密：只阻止本机浏览器储存记录、cookies 及输入资料；不会隐藏你的活动及 IP 地址，搜寻器仍可把它连到你的账户。

考试写法：Before spreading information, verify it with the official website or other credible sources, because false information may lead others to make wrong decisions.

ex.q: Amy gets a forwarded message saying all buses stop at 21:00 due to a typhoon. What should she do first?
ex.a:
1. Check the primary source with her friend.
2. Compare with the Hong Kong Observatory and other official/credible sources before deciding or forwarding.
ex.az:
1. 问清原始来源。
2. 与天文台等官方来源比较。

ex.q: An SMS asks Susan to pay customs duties at http://hkpost.com/9KcW3. Why should she not click it?
ex.a:
1. The real Hongkong Post domain is hongkongpost.hk, so this may be a phishing site.
2. She should call Hongkong Post to confirm.
ex.az:
1. 真正域名是 hongkongpost.hk，可能是钓鱼网站。
2. 应致电香港邮政查证。

ex.q: A student says: "In incognito mode, Google cannot see what I search." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: private browsing only stops the local browser storing data.
2. The search engine still sees the searches and your IP address.
ex.az:
1. 错误：只影响本机。
2. 搜寻器仍看到搜寻及 IP。

cards.en:
Analogy: misinformation spreads like a cold in a classroom: one person forwards it, then everyone has it, and it is hard to stop.

Misinformation = false or inaccurate information. Fake news = false information made to look like real news. Spreading or using it can cause:

  • Unnecessary panic – e.g. 2011: rumours that Japan's nuclear leak polluted sea salt (and that iodised salt protects from radiation) led to panic buying of salt in Hong Kong.
  • Monetary loss – fake Hongkong Post messages linked to phishing websites (fake sites that steal data) asking for delivery fees.
  • Reputational damage to people or companies.
  • Distrust in media, and others make wrong decisions.

Good habits: confirm the primary source (the original source), compare with official websites, don't forward unverified messages, use fact-checking services.

Exam wording: Misinformation may cause unnecessary panic, reputational damage, monetary loss and distrust in media, and lead others to make wrong decisions. Confirm the primary source before forwarding.
cards.zh:
比喻：假资讯像课室里的感冒：一人转发，人人都中，很难止住。

Misinformation＝错误资讯；fake news＝扮成真新闻的假资讯。后果：

  • 不必要恐慌：2011 年日本核事故「海盐受污染」谣言引发香港抢购盐
  • 金钱损失：假香港邮政讯息连到钓鱼网站要求付运费
  • 名誉受损
  • 不信任媒体、他人作出错误决定

好习惯：找第一手来源 primary source、对照官方网站、不转发未核实讯息、用事实查核服务。

Exam wording：Misinformation may cause unnecessary panic, reputational damage, monetary loss and distrust in media.

ex.q: Amy receives a forwarded message: all classes are cancelled tomorrow due to a typhoon. What should she do?
ex.a:
1. Find the primary source: who issued it?
2. Check official announcements (Hong Kong Observatory, Education Bureau, school website).
3. Do not forward it until verified, or others may make wrong decisions.
ex.az:
1. 找原始来源。
2. 对照天文台／教育局／学校公布。
3. 未核实不转发。

ex.q: An SMS claims to be from Hongkong Post: 'Your parcel is held. Pay HK$12 here: hkp-ost-pay.com'. State two possible impacts if many people believe it.
ex.a:
1. Monetary loss: victims pay and their credit card details are stolen on the phishing site.
2. Distrust: people stop trusting real messages from Hongkong Post.
ex.az:
1. 金钱损失：信用卡资料被盗。
2. 不再信任真正的邮政讯息。

ex.q: Joe forwards a health rumour and adds 'not sure if true, FYI'. He thinks this is harmless. Is it?
ex.a:
1. No. Many readers ignore the warning and still act on it.
2. It still spreads the misinformation further → possible panic or wrong decisions.
Right way: check first; if unverified, don't forward.
ex.az:
1. 有害。很多人忽略「未知真假」仍照做，资讯继续扩散。
2. 应先核实，不确定就不转发。

cards.t: Internet vs library as information sources
cards.tz: 互联网与图书馆作资料来源
cards.en:
Analogy: the Internet is a 24-hour market with everything, fresh and rotten; the library is a smaller shop where every item was inspected.

InternetLibrary / printed books
Search anywhere and anytime with Internet accessMust go there during opening hours
More likely to be up to datePrinted books may be old
Fast keyword search, multimedia, compare many sources quicklySlower to search
Anyone can publish → mixed qualityEdited and checked by publishers; stable content

Two common wrong beliefs:

  • Online information is NOT automatically free to use. It is still protected by copyright (the creator's legal right over the work).
  • Not only experts publish online: anyone can, so it is not automatically credible.

Exam wording: The Internet allows searching anywhere and anytime and its information is more likely to be up to date; however, anyone can publish online, so the information must be evaluated, and it is still protected by copyright.
cards.zh:
比喻：Internet 像 24 小时大街市，新鲜和腐坏的都有；图书馆像小店，每件货都经检查。

  • Internet：随时随地搜寻、较新、关键字搜寻快、多媒体、可快速比较；但任何人都可发布，质素参差
  • 图书馆／书本：要在开放时间去；可能较旧；但经出版者编辑审核、内容稳定

两个常见错误：网上资讯不是免费任用，仍受版权 copyright 保护；任何人都可在网上发布，不一定可信。

Exam wording：The Internet allows searching anywhere and anytime and is more likely to be up to date; but anyone can publish and content is still copyrighted.

ex.q: Which are advantages of the Internet over a library? (1) access anytime (2) more up to date (3) not copyrighted (4) only experts publish
ex.a:
1. (1) true.
2. (2) true.
3. (3) false – online content is still copyrighted.
4. (4) false – anyone can publish.
Answer: (1) and (2) only.
ex.az: 只有 (1)(2)。(3) 仍有版权；(4) 任何人都可发布。

ex.q: Give one situation where a library book is a better choice than a web search.
ex.a:
1. Writing a history essay that needs an authoritative, edited source.
2. The book is checked by the publisher and its content does not change, so it can be cited reliably.
ex.az: 写历史论文需要权威、经编辑的资料，书本内容稳定可引用。

ex.q: Why is the Internet better than a printed yearbook for finding this week's MTR fare changes?
ex.a:
1. Timeliness: websites can be updated immediately.
2. A printed book is fixed at printing time, so it cannot show this week's changes.
3. It can also be searched instantly from anywhere.
ex.az: 网站可即时更新，印刷书本内容固定；而且随时随地可查。

cards.en:
Analogy: a lesson with pictures, a short clip and spoken words is easier to follow than a page of text. Websites work the same way.

Multimedia = a mix of text, graphics, animation, video and audio. It can:

  • deliver ideas more easily;
  • attract users to stay longer;
  • support users with different learning styles and disabilities (audio for the visually impaired, captions for the hearing impaired).

The trade-off: media files are big. Compression makes them smaller. Lossless compression keeps every detail (best quality) but the file stays large, so it uses more transmission data and slows loading. Lossy compression throws away details people barely notice, so files are much smaller. Web designers pick formats that differ in colour depth, lossy/lossless, transparency, animation and browser compatibility.

Exam wording: Lossless compression offers the best quality but uses much more transmission data and slows down loading time; choose suitable file formats to reduce file size for faster transmission.
cards.zh:
比喻：有图、有短片、有讲解的课比一页纯文字易明白，网站也一样。

多媒体＝文字、图像、动画、影片、声音。好处：更易传达意念、吸引用户留得更久、照顾不同学习风格及残障人士（视障用声音、听障用字幕）。

取舍：媒体文件大。Lossless 无损压缩保留所有细节，画质最好但文件大，耗数据、载入慢；Lossy 有损压缩丢掉不易察觉的细节，文件细得多。设计师按色彩深度、有损／无损、透明、动画、兼容性选格式。

Exam wording：Lossless compression offers the best quality but uses much more transmission data and slows down loading time.

ex.q: Carol's phone data was used up early in the month. Suggest possible reasons.
ex.a:
1. Automatic photo backup over the mobile network.
2. Browsing social media full of videos/images.
3. Watching high-quality video streams.
4. Listening to lossless music online.
ex.az: 自动用流动数据备份相片、看多影片的社交网站、高清串流、无损音乐。

ex.q: Give two ways a museum website could use multimedia to help visitors with disabilities.
ex.a:
1. Audio descriptions of exhibits for visually impaired users.
2. Captions/subtitles on videos for hearing impaired users.
ex.az:
1. 为视障者提供语音导览。
2. 为听障者提供影片字幕。

ex.q: A designer uploads every photo uncompressed 'so the site looks best'. Explain the problem.
ex.a:
1. Uncompressed/lossless photos are very large.
2. Pages load slowly and use much more mobile data; users may leave.
Better: use lossy formats (JPG/WebP) at good quality – the difference is hard to see.
ex.az: 无压缩相片太大，载入慢、耗数据，用户会离开。应用 JPG/WebP 等有损格式。

demo.html:
Red panda

Red pandas live in mountain forests.

🍃

[Caption] Narrator: "The red panda eats mainly bamboo."

cards.en:
Analogy: image formats are like different bags: some are tiny but squash the contents (lossy), some keep everything perfect but are bulky (lossless), some have a see-through window (transparency).

FormatCompressionSpecial featuresBest for
JPGlossy, smallmost compatible; no transparencyphotos (social media, news)
PNGlossless, largertransparent backgroundscreenshots, images with text, icons
GIFlossless, max 256 colourssimple animation, transparencymemes, simple animations
APNGlosslessanimation with full colourstickers
WebPlossy or losslesssmaller with same visible quality; transparency + animationmodern websites (latest browsers)
SVGvector (not pixels)sharp at any sizeicons, logos
AVIFnew, open-sourceeven smaller; less supportfuture web images

SWF (Flash) is obsolete: Flash Player support ended at the end of 2020.

Exam wording: JPG uses lossy compression with small size and highest compatibility; PNG uses lossless compression and supports transparency; GIF supports animation but only 256 colours; WebP gives a smaller file size with the same quality.
cards.zh:
比喻：图像格式像不同袋子：有的细但会压扁东西（有损），有的完整但大（无损），有的有透明窗（透明背景）。

  • JPG：有损、细、兼容最好、不支援透明 → 相片
  • PNG：无损、较大、透明背景 → 截图、带文字图片
  • GIF：最多 256 色、简单动画 → meme
  • APNG：无损动画 → 贴图
  • WebP：同画质更细、支援透明及动画 → 新网站
  • SVG：向量图、任何大小都清晰 → icon、logo
  • AVIF：新、开源、更细、支援较少

SWF 已于 2020 年底淘汰。

Exam wording：JPG: lossy, small, most compatible; PNG: lossless, transparency; GIF: animation, 256 colours; WebP: smaller size with the same quality.

ex.q: Eva posts software screenshots with text on the option bars to her blog. Which format is best?
ex.a:
1. Screenshots have sharp text and flat colours.
2. PNG is lossless, so text stays sharp.
3. Flat colours compress well, so the PNG is not too big.
Answer: PNG.
ex.az: PNG：无损，文字清晰；平色画面压缩后不太大。

ex.q: A shop needs (a) a logo with a transparent background that stays sharp on any screen, (b) a short looping 'SALE' animation for old browsers, (c) a product photo. Choose formats.
ex.a:
(a) SVG – vector, sharp at any size, supports transparency.
(b) GIF – simple animation, supported everywhere.
(c) JPG (or WebP) – lossy, small file for a photo.
ex.az: (a) SVG (b) GIF (c) JPG/WebP

ex.q: Ivan saves a colourful sunset photo as GIF 'because GIF is small'. What goes wrong?
ex.a:
1. GIF has only 256 colours.
2. A sunset has thousands of smooth colour shades → banding (visible colour steps), looks worse.
3. The file may not even be smaller.
Right choice: JPG or WebP.
ex.az: GIF 只有 256 色，日落渐变会出现色带；应用 JPG/WebP。
